name: Die Cut Labels
seoTitle: Custom Die Cut Labels for Jars, Bottles and Boxes
seoDescription: Custom die cut labels cut to the shape of your artwork on paper, kraft, BOPP, vinyl or polyester. Rolls or sheets, free proof, free US shipping.
tagline: Product labels trimmed to your artwork shape, on paper, kraft, BOPP or vinyl, in rolls or sheets.
quickAnswer: Custom die cut labels are product labels cut to the outline of the artwork instead of a rectangle, oval or circle. We print them on matte or gloss paper, kraft, white or clear BOPP, white vinyl and polyester for jars, bottles, candle tins, soap wraps and bakery boxes. Pricing starts from $0.30 per label with a 100 piece minimum, and production takes 5 to 7 business days after proof approval.
highlights: Material: paper, kraft, BOPP, vinyl, polyester
Finish: gloss, matte or spot UV

sections.h2: Shaped labels for products that are not rectangles
sections.html:
A round candle tin, a tapered soap bar, a hexagonal honey jar. Standard label shapes fight these containers; a rectangle on a round lid leaves four corners hanging off the edge. A die cut label is cut to a shape you choose, usually the outline of the logo or illustration itself, so the artwork becomes the label and nothing else shows.

Our custom packaging labels are the closest sibling. That page covers rectangles, circles and ovals, often on rolls for a dispenser or an applicator, printed in the thousands for a product line. Die cut labels are for the product where the shape is part of the brand: a bee-shaped seal on a honey jar, a leaf on a tea tin, a scalloped badge on a jam lid. If your container is a plain cylinder and the artwork fits a rectangle, the custom packaging label page will cost less per piece because standard shapes nest tighter on the press sheet.

sections.h2: Which label stock survives your product
sections.html:
The stock matters more than the finish once a label meets oil, moisture or a refrigerator. Match it to what the container will go through after it leaves your bench.

StockMoisture and oilSurface it suitsBest for
Matte paperDry use onlyBoxes, bags, cardsBakery boxes, gift bags, retail tags
Kraft paperDry use onlyKraft boxes, tins, glassCandles, coffee bags, natural goods
White BOPPWater, oil and condensationGlass, PET, HDPE bottlesLotions, sauces, cold drinks
Clear BOPPWater and oilClear glass and plasticNo-label look on bottles and jars
White vinylWater, oil, outdoor sunMetal, plastic, curved tinsSoap wraps, outdoor products, equipment
Polyester (PET)Heat, chemicals, abrasionMetal, hard plasticAppliance and industrial labels

Paper and kraft are the lowest cost and print the warmest tones, but they wrinkle when wet. BOPP is the everyday choice for anything in a bathroom or a kitchen. Vinyl costs a little more and wraps around curves that BOPP fights.

sections.h2: Where a shaped label earns its cost
sections.html:
Die cutting adds a tooling step, so it pays off where the shape does a job that a rectangle cannot. We see it most on:

  • Candle tins and jar lids, where a round or badge-shaped label fills the lid edge to edge
  • Soap bars with a band or belly wrap cut to follow the curve of the bar
  • Bottle necks and hang-tag seals that need a tab or a hole punched in
  • Bakery boxes closed with a shaped seal that tears when the box is opened
  • Jam, honey and sauce jars where the logo silhouette replaces a front panel
  • Subscription boxes sealed with a mascot or icon that customers keep

Bath products deserve one extra note. A label on a shower shelf gets wet every day, so for those we start from BOPP or vinyl and laminate it; our waterproof sticker stock uses the same construction if you want to see what it withstands.

sections.h2: Choosing the right label in five decisions
sections.html:
Most of the back and forth on a label order happens before the proof. Settle these points first and the proof usually goes through on the first pass.

  1. Decide what the label touches: dry cardboard, glass that sweats, or a tin that gets handled with oily fingers. That picks the stock from the table above.
  2. Measure the flat area on the container. A label wider than the flat zone on a curved jar will fin at the edges, so size the label to that zone, not the whole face.
  3. Choose the shape and add a 0.0625 inch margin around the artwork unless you want the cut to run tight to the ink.
  4. Pick permanent adhesive for anything sold, or removable for jars customers reuse and gift packaging.
  5. Tell us how you apply them. Hand application works from sheets; a dispenser or applicator needs a roll with the unwind direction specified.

Send a PDF, AI, EPS, SVG or a 300 dpi PNG with the shape as a separate vector line if you have one. If not, we draw the cut line and show it on the proof.

sections.h2: Print details that matter on small labels
sections.html:
Labels run small, often under 3 inches, and that squeezes the type. Keep body text at 6 point or larger, and ingredient panels at 5 point minimum in a clean sans serif. Hairlines under 0.25 point drop out on uncoated paper. Barcodes print reliably at 80 percent scale or above with a quiet zone on both ends; put them on a white area, never across a photo.

Color behaves differently by stock. Kraft is brown, so colors print muted unless we lay a white ink underprint first, which we do on request. Clear BOPP needs the same white layer behind any color you want to look solid. On white paper and BOPP, Pantone matching holds within a close visual match, and the free proof shows the result before anything runs. Every sticker and label we make, including the shaped ones, starts from the same press setup described on our main custom sticker page.

sections.h2: Rolls, sheets and how the labels arrive
sections.html:
Sheets suit hand application and small batches; each sheet carries the labels on a split backing so a single label lifts with a thumbnail. Rolls suit a counter dispenser or an automatic applicator, wound on a 3 inch core with the unwind direction you specify. Either way the minimum is 100 labels per design, and several flavors or scents of the same shape can be combined on one order.

Production is 5 to 7 business days from proof approval, delivery is 8 to 10 business days by FedEx, and shipping is free within the United States. Store unused rolls flat in the bag they arrive in; paper labels pick up humidity in a garage and curl at the corners within a few weeks.

faqs.q: What is the difference between die cut labels and regular packaging labels?
faqs.a: The cut. A regular packaging label is a rectangle, circle or oval, usually on a roll. A die cut label is cut to the outline of the artwork or any custom shape, so the logo itself becomes the label. Same stocks, same print, but a shaped label needs its own cutting die and nests less efficiently.

faqs.q: Can custom die cut labels go on a curved jar or bottle?
faqs.a: Yes, if the label fits the flat zone of the curve. A jar that tapers will push a wide label into fins at the edges, so we size the label to the straight part of the wall. For tight curves, white vinyl conforms better than BOPP or paper, and a narrower belly band beats a tall front panel.

faqs.q: Which die cut label stock is safe around oils and lotions?
faqs.a: White or clear BOPP, laminated. BOPP is a plastic film, so body oil, lotion and essential oils bead on it instead of soaking in and staining. Paper and kraft absorb oil and go translucent within days. For soap bars that sit wet in a dish, step up to white vinyl with a laminate.

faqs.q: Will a kraft die cut label print bright colors?
faqs.a: Only with a white ink underprint. Kraft is brown, so colors printed directly on it come out muted, which many natural brands like. If you want a red or a sky blue to read true, we print a white layer under those areas first. Black and single dark colors look sharp on kraft without any underprint.

faqs.q: Can die cut labels be supplied on rolls for a label applicator?
faqs.a: Yes. Rolls come on a 3 inch core with the unwind direction you specify, which matters because an applicator feeds from one side only. Tell us the applicator model or the direction code on the quote request. Hand-applied orders usually ship on sheets with a split backing instead.

faqs.q: How small can the text be on a die cut label?
faqs.a: Keep body copy at 6 point or above, and ingredient or legal panels no smaller than 5 point in a clean sans serif. Reversed white text out of a dark color should stay at 7 point. Lines thinner than 0.25 point fill in on uncoated paper, so build fine detail from solid shapes rather than hairlines.

faqs.q: Do die cut labels survive a refrigerator or freezer?
faqs.a: BOPP and vinyl labels do, provided they go on at room temperature and cure for 24 hours before the cold. Condensation during thawing is the real test, and a laminated BOPP label passes it. Paper labels wrinkle and lift once they get wet, so keep paper for dry shelf products.

faqs.q: Can die cut labels be made in clear BOPP?
faqs.a: Yes. Clear BOPP gives a no-label look on glass and clear plastic, with only the artwork showing. Colors go translucent on clear film, so we print a white ink layer under any area that should look solid. We also laminate it so fingerprints and oil wipe off without marking the print.

faqs.q: What is the smallest order of custom die cut labels?
faqs.a: 100 labels per design. Several flavors, scents or sizes that share one shape can go on a single order, and pricing starts from $0.30 per label depending on size, stock and quantity. A run of 100 is enough for a market stall test; larger runs bring the unit cost down.

faqs.q: How do I order die cut labels in several flavors or scents?
faqs.a: Send one file per variant, named by flavor, and tell us the quantity of each. If the shape and size are the same across variants, they share the cutting die and run as one job, which keeps the cost close to a single-design order. Each variant still gets its own proof so you can check the ingredient text.

faqs.q: Are die cut labels suitable for jars and bakery boxes that hold food?
faqs.a: Yes for the outside of the packaging, which is where the label sits. The adhesive bonds to the box or jar, not the food. For bakery boxes, matte paper takes a stamp or a handwritten date well; for jars that get wiped or chilled, choose BOPP so the label stays flat and readable.

faqs.q: How long does a die cut label order take to arrive?
faqs.a: Plan on 8 to 10 business days from proof approval to your door. That covers 5 to 7 days of printing and cutting plus FedEx delivery, which is free within the United States. A reorder of a label we have already cut moves faster because the die and the proof already exist.
